results.content:
We then introduce a learnable spatio-temporal rotation matrix to encode spatial information, calculated as follows:

$$
\mathbf{R}_{\Phi(x,y)} = \begin{bmatrix}
\cos \phi_1(x, y)\theta_1 & -\sin \phi_1(x, y)\theta_1 & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\
\sin \phi_1(x, y)\theta_1 & \cos \phi_1(x, y)\theta_1 & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots & \vdots \\
0 & 0 & \cdots & \cos \phi_{d/2}(x, y)\theta_{d/2} & -\sin \phi_{d/2}(x, y)\theta_{d/2} \\
0 & 0 & \cdots & \sin \phi_{d/2}(x, y)\theta_{d/2} & \cos \phi_{d/2}(x, y)\theta_{d/2}
\end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}
$$ (1)

where $\phi_k(x, y)$ is the $k$-th element of $\Phi(x, y)$, $\theta_1, \theta_2, \ldots, \theta_{d/2}$ are frequency weights, and $\theta_k = 10000^{-2k/d}$.
results.route_rationale: Block-diagonal matrix asserted to be a rotation matrix in R^{d×d}; orthogonality of the 2×2 rotation blocks is a formalizable, non-trivial trigonometric claim.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the claim that the block-diagonal spatio-temporal rotation matrix of Eq (1) is a rotation matrix. Proved: (1) each 2×2 block R(α) = [[cos α, -sin α], [sin α, cos α]] is orthogonal, R(α)ᵀ R(α) = I, with det R(α) = 1; (2) the block-diagonal assembly of any number of such blocks is orthogonal. The block entries are read as cos(φ_k(x,y)θ_k) etc., matching the appendix Eq (7) reading (the frequency θ_k multiplies the angle inside the trig function). All three theorems compiled cleanly via lake env lean (exit 0, no errors, no sorryAx); axioms are the standard [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

results.location: C The Proof of TRIE to Capture Relative Spatial Information
results.content:
Based on the matrix multiplication of the attention mechanism, we apply $\mathbf{R}_{\Phi(x,y)}$ to the query and key, allowing the model to effectively capture the relative information $\mathbf{R}_{\Phi(x_i - x_j, y_i - y_j)}$ between trajectory points.

$$
\begin{align}
\mathbf{q}_i \cdot \mathbf{k}_j^{\top} &= (\mathbf{R}_{\Phi(x_i, y_i)} \mathbf{W}_q \mathbf{e}_i)^{\top} \cdot (\mathbf{R}_{\Phi(x_j, y_j)} \mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{e}_j) \\
&= \mathbf{e}_i^{\top} \mathbf{W}_q^{\top} \mathbf{R}_{\Phi(x_i, y_i)}^{\top} (\mathbf{R}_{\Phi(x_j, y_j)} \mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{e}_j) \\
&= \mathbf{e}_i^{\top} \mathbf{W}_q^{\top} \begin{bmatrix}
\circled{1} & \circled{2} & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\
\circled{3} & \circled{4} & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots & \vdots \\
0 & 0 & \cdots & \circled{5} & \circled{6} \\
0 & 0 & \cdots & \circled{7} & \circled{8}
\end{bmatrix} \mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{e}_j \\
&= \mathbf{e}_i^{\top} \mathbf{W}_q^{\top} \begin{bmatrix}
\cos(\phi_1[(x_i, y_i) - (x_j, y_j)]\theta_1) & \sin(\phi_1[(x_i, y_i) - (x_j, y_j)]\theta_1) & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\
-\sin(\phi_1[(x_i, y_i) - (x_j, y_j)]\theta_1) & \cos(\phi_1[(x_i, y_i) - (x_j, y_j)]\theta_1) & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots & \vdots \\
0 & 0 & \cdots & \cos(\phi_{d/2}[(x_i, y_i) - (x_j, y_j)]\theta_{d/2}) & \sin(\phi_{d/2}[(x_i, y_i) - (x_j, y_j)]\theta_{d/2}) \\
0 & 0 & \cdots & -\sin(\phi_{d/2}[(x_i, y_i) - (x_j, y_j)]\theta_{d/2}) & \cos(\phi_{d/2}[(x_i, y_i) - (x_j, y_j)]\theta_{d/2})
\end{bmatrix} \mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{e}_j \\
&= \mathbf{e}_i^{\top} \mathbf{W}_q^{\top} \mathbf{R}_{\Phi(x_i, y_i) - \Phi(x_j, y_j)}^{\top} \mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{e}_j \\
&= \mathbf{e}_i^{\top} \mathbf{W}_q^{\top} \mathbf{R}_{\Phi(x_i - x_j, y_i - y_j)}^{\top} \mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{e}_j,
\end{align}
$$

where $\circled{1} = \cos(\phi_1(x_i, y_i)\theta_1)\cos(\phi_1(x_j, y_j)\theta_1) + \sin(\phi_1(x_i, y_i)\theta_1)\sin(\phi_1(x_j, y_j)\theta_1)$, and similarly for $\circled{2}, \ldots, \circled{8}$.
results.route_rationale: The derivation's correctness turns on the rotation-matrix identity R(α)ᵀ R(β) = R(α-β)ᵀ (trig identities) and on the linearity of Φ — both formalizable.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the two load-bearing steps of the Appendix C derivation (Eq (8)). (1) Rotation identity: for 2×2 rotation matrices R(θ) = [[cos θ, -sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]], R(α)ᵀ R(β) = R(α-β)ᵀ; and the block-diagonal analogue R_{Φ_i}ᵀ R_{Φ_j} = R_{Φ_i - Φ_j}ᵀ. This is the step from line 2 to line 5 of Eq (8) — the circled entries of Eq (9) are exactly the trig identities cos(a-b) = cos a cos b + sin a sin b and sin(a-b) = sin a cos b − cos a sin b. (2) Linearity of Φ: since Φ(x,y) = W_Φ (x‖y) is a linear projection, Φ(x_i,y_i) − Φ(x_j,y_j) = Φ(x_i−x_j, y_i−y_j); this is the step from line 5 to line 6. Both formalised claims compiled cleanly via lake env lean (exit 0, no errors, no sorryAx); axioms are the standard [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The derivation is mathematically sound.

summary: Transversal math verification of TransferTraj (NeurIPS 2025), a vehicle trajectory learning model. The paper is an ML systems paper: most of its display mathematics is architecture notation (POI/road modality sets, relative coordinates, query/key/value definitions, SC-MoE output, noisy top-K gating, loss functions) and experimental numeric tables — content the skill directs to skip. Two self-contained, formally checkable mathematical objects were extracted and routed to verify-math-lean against the shared MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper project: (1) paper::EQUATION::0, the block-diagonal 'spatio-temporal rotation matrix' R_{Φ(x,y)} of Eq (1), asserted to be a rotation matrix in R^{d×d} with θ_k = 10000^{-2k/d}; and (2) paper::PROOF::0, the Appendix C derivation (Eq (8)) showing the rotated query-key dot product reduces to the relative rotation R_{Φ(x_i-x_j, y_i-y_j)}^{\top}. Both were formalised in Lean 4 and PASSED: the 2×2 rotation blocks are orthogonal with det 1, their block-diagonal assembly is orthogonal, the rotation identity R(α)ᵀ R(β) = R(α-β)ᵀ (and its block analogue) holds, and Φ linearity justifies the final step. No verify-math fallbacks were needed (no FAILED Lean results), so there was no verifier disagreement. No findings. The only observation worth noting is a notation ambiguity in Eq (1): 'cos φ_k(x, y)θ_k' is shorthand that the appendix Eq (7) resolves to cos(φ_k(x,y)θ_k); under the literal reading θ_k·cos(φ_k) the block would not be a rotation matrix (det = θ_k²), but the appendix clarifies the intended reading, and the Lean formalisation used that clarified reading. Verdict: NO_ERRORS with confidence 0.8 — the two formalizable mathematical claims are machine-checked clean, but the coverage is limited because most of the paper's content is non-formalisable architecture/experimental material. The shared Lean project was reused (it already held proofs for other papers) and was therefore kept on disk (lean_project_kept = true); proofs saved under MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper/Paper/Verified/TransferTraj__EQUATION__0.lean and TransferTraj__PROOF__0.lean.
